title: Maplewood Retail - Procurement MSA/DPA/SLAs Review
next_steps: Redwood to share redlined MSA + DPA by Tue 2027-02-25
SE team to run 24h benchmark with sample traffic (Priya) and share results
Schedule onboarding kickoff after legal sign-off (Sophie to coordinate)
action_items: Priya Rao: run dedicated vs hosted latency/cost benchmark with 100k tokens/day sample (due 2027-03-01)
Liam Chen: send pricing deck and draft MSA/DPA to Ethan (due 2027-02-25)
Sophie Nguyen: schedule onboarding kickoff and share onboarding checklist (due 2027-03-04)
summary: Procurement-legal call to review MSA/DPA, SLAs, and pricing for a Dedicated + Private deployment for Maplewood Retail. Key concerns: data residency, SOC 2 controls, KMS/HSM integration, support SLAs, and pricing approvals. Redwood AE/SE pair walked through technical appendices and proposed pilot. Agreed next steps: redline exchange, 24h benchmark, and onboarding kickoff contingent on legal sign-off.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes scheduled. quick roll call?
[00:12] Grace (Procurement): Grace here.
[00:15] Ethan (Legal): Ethan on the line.
[00:18] Maya (CTO): Maya, hi.
[00:20] Omar (Platform): Omar, infra eng.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya from Redwood, hi all.
[00:25] Sophie (CSM): Sophie, CSM.
[00:28] Liam: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: Liam to cover pricing and MSA/DPA high-level, Priya will do technical appendix and SLAs, then we take questions and agree next steps.
[01:10] Grace: Sounds good. From our side we have procurement and legal here. main things for us, data residency, auditability, and, you know, certs. SOC2, ISO, and the whole SSO and SAML story.
[01:35] Liam: Totally. On SOC 2, we are SOC 2 Type II, we can share the report under NDA. We also have an ISO27001 cert in progress. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC and can do SCIM for user provisioning.
[02:05] Ethan: When you say "share the report under NDA" — is that already public or do we need a separate NDA?
[02:12] Sophie: We can share the SOC 2 report via our secure portal. standard process is an NDA or an existing proc portal access, happy to use your preferred mechanism.
[02:26] Maya: On the infra side — we need to confirm VPC peering and KMS integration. Our security team requires customer-managed KMS, HSM ideally. Does Redwood support bringing your own KMS?
[02:42] Priya: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and can integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSMs. We'll attach the KMS technical note in the appendix. One note — if you want Dedicated hosted with BYOK, there are a few network setup steps we typically run through.
[03:10] Omar: For the PCI/sensitive PII flows — can you confirm whether data persists on the Redwood side? We need to know retention and option to disable persistent storage.
[03:22] Liam: Good call — for Dedicated and Private options, we can provide options: short-term KV cache only vs persist logs. Our standard Hosted API retains logs for X days by default but enterprise customers can opt-out or request data purge policies. We'll include DPA language to reflect that.
[03:40] Ethan: In terms of liability and indemnities in the MSA — are there any carve-outs we should be aware of? The sample MSA had the standard caps but we need to see if there's enterprise-level SLA credits spelled out.
[03:52] Liam: We include SLA credits for uptime windows on Dedicated. Standard hosted SLAs differ. For Dedicated we can discuss custom SLA and higher uptime targets in a committed capacity contract. We'll note that pricing changes if you want an SLA-backed commit.
[04:12] Grace: Pricing is a big one. Our procurement needs list pricing for pilot, then full roll-out numbers. Can you remind the model — is it per-token for hosted and per-hour for dedicated?
[04:24] Liam: Yes, hosted is usage-based per-token/per-embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity monthly (GPU hours) with burst options. We provided a preliminary price sheet last week. I'll resend a cleaned up deck with both pilot and scale scenarios.
[04:46] Priya: If helpful, we can run a 24-hour benchmark with a sample workload to show expected latency and effective cost per 1k tokens across both modes — that typically helps procurement choose the right economic model.
[05:02] Maya: That would be helpful. We care about 95th percentile latency under our peak traffic patterns; if you can show numbers for both quantized and FP16 models that would be ideal.
[05:15] Priya: Absolutely — we'll run dedicated and hosted variants, and also include our quantization matrix (int8 / q4 / fp16) tradeoffs for quality vs cost.
[05:28] Omar: On the networking side, how do you handle egress and routing for regional data residency? We have EU customers and need EU-only processing.
[05:40] Liam: For Private deployments you can pin regions, and for Dedicated we can route traffic into EU capacity. We also have an option to deploy in-customer VPC for air-gapped or on-prem airgap cases.
[05:56] Grace: About the DPA — there was a clause about subprocessors. Can you confirm the list of subprocessors and whether you accept customer-specific subprocessor additions?
[06:08] Sophie: We'll share the current subprocessor list; additions can be handled via DPA addendum. We try to be transparent and include a notice period for changes.
[06:20] Ethan: Also looking at eDiscovery and audit logs — we need audit trails for all admin actions and API calls for 12 months. Is that available?
[06:30] Priya: Yes, per-route audit logging is supported and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch. Retention windows can be configured but longer retention may be part of a premium add-on.
[06:46] Liam: Quick pause — any questions before we dig into the MSA redlines?
[06:52] Grace: No, go ahead.
[06:58] Liam: We've sent a draft MSA and DPA — in the draft we typically keep liability caps tied to fees and have SLA credits spelled out. We can be flexible on SLA language for enterprise customers; we'll need a committed monthly spend for the higher SLA.
[07:18] Ethan: On indemnity for IP — if there's a third-party claim on model outputs, how is that handled?
[07:25] Priya: Model outputs are a bit tricky — our standard is that customers control prompts and outputs, but we do include language about copyright claims. For certain higher-risk use cases we recommend a model audit and can provide model provenance docs.
[07:40] Maya: Might need that for our product team.
[07:44] Liam: Noted — we'll include model provenance and a short note on usage guidelines.
[07:50] Grace: Turning to timeline — procurement wants pricing approvals by end of next week to start pilot by March 7th. Is that feasible?
[07:59] Liam: Yes, we can aim to have redlined MSA/DPA back by Feb 25th and the pilot can kick off the week of March 1st, pending legal. Priya can run the benchmark before that.
[08:12] Omar: For the benchmark, what environment? Will you spin up a Dedicated pool or simulate hosted traffic? We want realistic tail latency.
[08:20] Priya: We'll provision a small Dedicated pool to replicate your committed config and run the load against both dedicated and hosted variants to compare. We'll include p95/p99, avg, and cost per 1k tokens.
[08:34] Ethan: On prices for pilot — do you offer a trial credit or discounted pilot rate?
[08:40] Liam: We typically offer pilot pricing discounts and credits for new enterprise pilots; I'll include a pilot pricing line-item in the sheet.
[08:51] Grace: Good. On SLAs, specifically RTO/RPO for incidents — we need incident response within 1 hour and a postmortem within 72 hours. Is that in line with your support tiers?
[09:02] Sophie: Our premium SLA includes 1-hour incident response and 2-hour escalation. Postmortems within 72 hours are standard for severity 1 incidents; we'll call that out in the SLA appendix.
[09:16] Liam: Also note backup and restore for Private deployments — we support snapshotting config and model artifacts, customer retains keys.
[09:28] Maya: Regarding the onboarding checklist — what's the expected engineering effort on our side? We have a small infra team.
[09:36] Sophie: For a standard Dedicated + VPC setup expect 2-3 weeks of part-time work for network and KMS setup; we'll provide a checklist and runbooks. If you go Private on-prem it can be 4-6 weeks depending on procurement of hardware.
[09:52] Omar: Any required firewall ports or egress rules?
[09:55] Priya: We'll provide a network playbook, but typically outbound HTTPS to specific endpoints, and for VPC peering some private ranges.
[10:05] Grace: OK, can we talk risk allocation — if we need certain indemnities or more favorable caps, what is the posture?
[10:12] Liam: We can negotiate a higher cap tied to committed spend; for very large caps we need sign-off from finance/legal. We'll take any redline and escalate internally.
[10:24] Ethan: We'll send redlines. One ask — can you accept EU data residency and be explicit for EU customers in the DPA?
[10:32] Sophie: Yes, we can add an EU residency subsection and specify processing locations for your tenant.
[10:40] Maya: Any examples of customers with similar requirements?
[10:43] Liam: Yes — we have a few enterprise retail customers in EU running Dedicated with BYOK and VPC peering. We'll share anonymized references.
[10:55] Grace: Great. About subprocessor notification windows? Procurement prefers 30 days notice and option to opt-out for new subprocessors.
[11:03] Ethan: That was our legal ask.
[11:05] Sophie: We typically do 30 days; opt-out can be reviewed case-by-case. We'll propose language in the DPA.
[11:14] Liam: We're at about 40 minutes left, but I want to make sure we capture the key next steps.
[11:21] Grace: Yes.
[11:23] Liam: Recap: Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA by Feb 25th; Priya to run 24h benchmark and share p95/p99 and cost comparisons by March 1st; Sophie to schedule onboarding kickoff after legal sign-off. Customer will return redlines to Ethan. Any additions?
[11:40] Ethan: add audit log retention 12 months in DPA.
[11:44] Priya: noted.
[11:46] Omar: I'll provide sample traffic profile and a list of endpoints to simulate by Monday.
[11:50] Liam: Perfect. We'll attach links to docs: security portal (link: https://redwood.example.com/security), draft MSA (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/msa-draft), pricing deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/pricing).
[12:05] Grace: Thanks everyone. We'll expect the redline and pilot pricing.
[12:10] Liam: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with attachments and schedule the benchmark window.
[12:15] Sophie: Thanks.
[12:16] Meeting ends.
